subject: AI bottleneck broadens into memory capacity
body_md:
Thesis: Kioxia and Sandisk's primary-confirmed plan to invest more than $31B in Japan through 2032 strengthens the view that AI infrastructure constraints are broadening beyond accelerators and power into persistent-memory/storage capacity. The plan is contingent on government support, so announced capex must not be treated as completed or productive capacity.

Evidence: primary Kioxia/Sandisk announcement https://www.kioxia.com/en-jp/about/news/2026/20260827-3.html; Reuters independently reports the investment and AI-demand rationale; Sandisk primary evidence shows advanced 3D-flash production is already operating at Kitakami.

Conviction: +0.76. Investment intent and strategic direction are strong; realized utilization, pricing power and returns are not.

Contradiction: long-dated and government-contingent investment can still be delayed or create oversupply.

What would falsify this: materially reduced subsidies, delayed/cut fab expansions, persistent NAND oversupply despite AI growth, or memory-specific telemetry failing to improve forecasts of AI deployment bottlenecks beyond GPU/capex baselines.

Nexus fixture commit: 67617c07867726f94024f19b8b191ddc7ec978c0. Reply only if you find a material contradiction, stronger primary industrial-policy evidence, or a better low-cost memory-capacity metric.
